backlog.spec: Replace construct_packing with a multi-start optimizer: variables are (x,y,r) for 26 circles; maximize sum r using scipy.optimize.minimize(method='SLSQP') with vectorized inequality constraints (pairwise dist - ri - rj >= 0, r<=x<=1-r, r<=y<=1-r) and analytic jacobians. Start from random centers with small radii, seed fixed, keep best within ~200s. Shrink radii by 1e-12 before returning and make run_packing return the sum of the shrunk radii.
backlog.title: SLSQP joint optimization from random starts

backlog.spec: Initialize centers from a perturbed hexagonal lattice (rows of 5,5,5,5,6 or 6,5,6,5,4 variants, trimmed to 26 points) scaled to fit the square, add Gaussian jitter of 0.02, initial radii from compute_max_radii, then run SLSQP joint (x,y,r) optimization. Try many jitter seeds and keep the best valid result.
backlog.title: Hex-grid initialization with jitter then SLSQP

backlog.spec: After any center optimization, fix centers and solve the LP max sum r subject to r_i<=border distance, r_i+r_j<=d_ij using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). Alternate: LP for radii, then SLSQP step on centers, repeating until convergence. Shrink by 1e-12 at the end.
backlog.title: LP radii refinement on fixed centers

backlog.spec: Use a custom basin-hopping loop: perturb 1-3 random circles (relocate to random positions) or all by small noise, re-optimize with SLSQP from the current best, accept if improved (or with Metropolis criterion at small temperature). Run until a 200s time budget is used with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Basin hopping on centers

backlog.spec: Minimize -sum r + mu*(sum overlap^2 + sum boundary violation^2) using L-BFGS-B on (x,y,r) with analytic gradients; increase mu from 1e1 to 1e6 over stages. Then finalise with SLSQP polish and radii shrink for strict validity.
backlog.title: Penalty method with L-BFGS and annealed penalty

backlog.spec: Run 300 short SLSQP runs (maxiter ~40) from random starts, rank by sum radii, then fully polish top 5 with maxiter 500 and tight ftol. Returns the best valid one.
backlog.title: Many cheap starts, polish top-k

backlog.spec: Initialize 4 large circles at the square corners (radius ~0.13), 12 circles along edges, and the rest in an interior grid with larger radii at the center; random jitter; then SLSQP. Multiple seeds.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored structure init

backlog.spec: Try concentric ring initial structures with different ring counts (e.g. 1/8/17, 1/6/12/7, 2/9/15) mapped into the square with a slight stretch toward the square, then SLSQP. Loop over variants and jitters, keep best.
backlog.title: Ring-based init (1+ 6 + 12 + 7 variants)

backlog.spec: Initialize radii from a bimodal distribution (some big ~0.15, many small ~0.07) and centers by Poisson-disc-like sampling with larger circles placed first; then SLSQP. Encourages variable-sized solutions.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted size diversity init

backlog.spec: From the current best solution, remove the circle with the smallest radius and reinsert it at the largest hole (found by evaluating a fine grid for max distance to circle boundaries and walls), re-run SLSQP. Iterate as a local search move for the time budget.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Impose mirror symmetry about the diagonal (13 circles pairs/on-axis) by optimizing half the variables, via SLSQP, then release the symmetry and polish with a full SLSQP. Test also 180-degree rotational symmetry (13 pairs).
backlog.title: Symmetry-constrained search

backlog.spec: Optimize with a log-barrier objective -sum r - t*sum log(slack) using Newton/L-BFGS, decreasing t geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-9, starting from a feasible point (small radii). Final SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Soft-min log-barrier interior point

backlog.spec: Use scipy trust-constr with NonlinearConstraint providing sparse jacobian for pair constraints only on near neighbors (d<0.4), recomputing the neighbor list each outer round. Compare to SLSQP on speed and quality.
backlog.title: trust-constr with sparse constraints

backlog.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs with center distance < 2.5*(ri+rj)+0.1 at each outer restart, re-solve and verify full feasibility; reduces 325 constraints to ~100, allowing many more restarts within time.
backlog.title: Active-set neighbor pruning for SLSQP

backlog.spec: SA over centers only; the objective is the LP-optimal sum of radii (linprog highs). Move: gaussian step on one circle with temperature decreasing 0.02 to 0.0005. Finish with SLSQP joint polish.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing on centers with LP radii

backlog.spec: Simulate circles with radii grown at rate proportional to free space, pairwise repulsive forces on overlap, and wall forces, damping; shrink step size over iterations. Use the result as initial guess for SLSQP.
backlog.title: Physics repulsion with growing radii

backlog.spec: Iterated local search: after each SLSQP, perturb all centers with noise sigma cycling over [0.01,0.03,0.06], reoptimize, keep if better. Reset to the best after 15 non-improvements.
backlog.title: Perturbation of the best with larger noise schedule

backlog.spec: Local-search move: pick two adjacent circles with different radii, swap their centers, reoptimize with SLSQP briefly. Accept improvements. Helps rearrange size ordering.
backlog.title: Swap sizes of neighboring circles

backlog.spec: Enumerate row-count patterns such as [5,5,6,5,5], [6,5,5,5,5], [4,6,6,6,4], [5,6,4,6,5] summing to 26, place circles evenly in rows with offsets, jitter, SLSQP. Keep best over patterns and seeds.
backlog.title: Different row structure inits (5 rows pattern)

backlog.spec: Stage 1: optimize centers with all radii constrained equal (maximin-like) by SLSQP to get a well-spread layout; stage 2: free radii and centers jointly via SLSQP. Multiple random starts.
backlog.title: Two-stage: equal radii then free radii

backlog.spec: In early SLSQP runs add a bound r_i >= 0.03 to prevent degenerate tiny circles, then relax to r_i >= 0 in the final polish. Reduces getting stuck in poor local optima.
backlog.title: Radius lower-bound regularization to avoid zero circles

backlog.spec: Initially maximize sum w_i r_i with random weights w_i in [0.8,1.2] to bias different size distributions, then reset weights to 1 and polish. Many random weight draws.
backlog.title: Weighted objective exploration

backlog.spec: Use scipy differential_evolution on 52 center coordinates with LP radii as the fitness for a few generations (small popsize), then polish the best with SLSQP. Budget-limited with fixed seed.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over coarse parameters

backlog.spec: After optimization, compute radii as min(current r, wall distance, half of (d_ij - other)) and subtract 1e-12 from all; verify with exact pair checks in double precision, iterating shrink by factor 1-1e-12 until all valid. Return sum of the final radii.
backlog.title: Precise final validity shrink

backlog.spec: Rewrite constraint and jacobian generation with precomputed index arrays (np.triu_indices) and vectorized numpy, no Python loops, so each SLSQP run costs ~0.2s, allowing ~1000 restarts in the time budget.
backlog.title: Fast vectorized numpy constraints

backlog.spec: Compute (not hard-code) an initial layout: a 5x5 square grid with one extra circle inserted at a gap, with radii tuned by LP, followed by strong random perturbation and SLSQP. Multiple seeds.
backlog.title: Seed using known-style hybrid layout

backlog.spec: Keep a list of sum-of-radii values and sorted radii signatures of found optima; reject restarts that converge to an already found signature and bias new perturbations to larger magnitude, spreading exploration.
backlog.title: Tabu on previous local optima

backlog.spec: From the best solution, scale all radii by 0.9, then apply random centre jitter, and re-optimize with SLSQP. This relaxes the contacts so circles can rearrange, followed by regrowing. Repeat.
backlog.title: Shrink-and-grow cycles

backlog.spec: Wrap everything in a loop using time.time() with a total budget of 220 s, allocating 60 percent to global random starts, 40 percent to perturbation of the best; stops safely before the limit and always returns the best valid packing found so far.
backlog.title: Time-aware restart controller

backlog.spec: Remove the two smallest circles and the one most constrained neighbor, then reinsert three circles in the three largest empty holes (greedy via grid search), reoptimize with SLSQP. Accept if improved.
backlog.title: Remove-two-add-two rearrangement

backlog.spec: After the best SLSQP result is chosen, recompute radii with lp_radii on the final centers (the LP is exact for fixed centers). Then do a vectorized safe shrink: compute pairwise violations and scale radii so that r_i + r_j <= d_ij*(1-1e-12) and r_i <= border distance, then multiply by (1-1e-12) instead of 1-1e-9. Verify the packing in double precision with zero tolerance and fall back to the old radii if the check fails. This gains a few 1e-9 and cleans up SLSQP constraint slop.
backlog.title: Final LP polish plus tight margin

backlog.spec: Add an init generator that places circles in concentric rings around the square center, with counts drawn at random from variants such as (1,6,12,7), (1,7,11,7), (2,8,16) and (4,9,13). The ring radii are random in [0.15,0.45] and each ring has a random phase. Add Gaussian jitter of 0.01, clip to [0.05,0.95], then run the existing SA, SLSQP and shrink-and-grow pipeline. Choose the init type at random per start, half hex-row and half ring, with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Ring-based inits (1+6+12+7 variants)

backlog.spec: Initialise with 4 large circles near the corners (centers about 0.12-0.15 from each corner), 4 medium circles at edge midpoints, and the other 18 on a jittered hex-like interior lattice with random smaller spacing. Seed SLSQP radii from the LP radii for these centers. Run the existing SA, SLSQP and shrink-and-grow pipeline, picking this init in about half of the starts.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored big circles init

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP result, loop over several iterations: find the circle with the smallest radius (or the k smallest, k random in 1-3), delete it, and reinsert it at a random point from the largest empty holes. Find holes by sampling 2000 random points and taking the ones with the largest distance-to-nearest-circle surface (min over d - r_j and the border distance). Re-run SLSQP with maxiter 200 from the modified state and accept only if the sum of radii improves. Run this for the best start until the time budget (about 200s total) is used.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert worst circle

backlog.spec: Add a cheap global stage. Minimise -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared pair overlaps max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 + sum of squared border violations) with L-BFGS-B over (x, y, r), using analytic gradients vectorized with triu indices. Anneal mu through 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 from random hex-jittered starts, using about 50 starts. Pass the best 3 to the SLSQP polish in place of the SA stage.
backlog.title: Penalty L-BFGS with annealed overlap penalty

backlog.spec: Change sa_centers to use steps=6000, T0=0.01, T1=0.0001 and sigma = 0.003 + 0.02*(T/T0). Pick the moved circle with a bias towards the smallest-radius circles 50% of the time. Increase the time cap in SA to 60s per start, and use 3 starts instead of 4. To speed it up, replace the full linprog with warm-started evaluation only on the changed circle's neighbours if possible. Otherwise keep the LP as is.
backlog.title: Slower SA with smaller moves and more steps

backlog.spec: Extend hex_jitter to choose randomly among many row structures that sum to 26: [5,5,5,5,6], [6,5,6,5,4], [5,6,5,6,4], [4,5,4,5,4,4] with 6 rows, [6,5,5,5,5], [3,4,3,4,3,4,3,3,3] style variants and 6-row patterns like [4,5,4,5,4,4]. Use a random jitter sigma in [0.01,0.04] and a random flip or transpose. Run 6 starts with a shorter SA (800 steps) so that more topologies are explored. Keep the best.
backlog.title: Row pattern sweep inits

backlog.spec: Add a second SA move type chosen 20% of the time: swap the positions of two nearby circles of different LP radii, or move a circle to a random location chosen from a hole. Since the LP re-optimises radii, swapping position effectively changes the size pattern. Keep the other move type as is. Accept with the Metropolis rule on LP sum. This lets SA change the topology that Gaussian moves rarely change.
backlog.title: Swap-radii and neighbor moves in SA

backlog.spec: Stage 1: for random jittered starts, maximise the common radius with SLSQP (equal circles, 26 circles, maxiter 100), which gives a well spread layout. Stage 2: perturb the centers with 0.01 noise and run the free-radius SLSQP and then the SA/shrink-and-grow cycles. Use this as the init for half the starts, with the rest hex-jitter.
backlog.title: Two-stage equal-radius then free

backlog.spec: After the 4 starts, take the best solution and run iterated local search until 200s total. Each iteration picks 2-4 random circles and relocates them to random positions (or jitters all centers with sigma 0.03), sets the radii to 0.8 of their values, runs SLSQP with maxiter 200 and accepts it if the sum improves (or with small probability if worse by less than 0.002). Keep the global best and the final validity shrink.
backlog.title: Best-state perturbation with iterated large kicks

backlog.spec: After the best SLSQP result is chosen, recompute radii with lp_radii(centers) (fixed centers, exact LP). Then verify pairwise and wall feasibility in double precision and shrink radii by only 1e-12 relative (instead of 1e-9) plus a pairwise safe_radii check. Keep the LP result only if its sum is >= the SLSQP sum, otherwise fall back to the SLSQP radii. Wrap the code in try/except so a failure returns the old valid answer.
backlog.title: Final LP radius polish with tight margin

backlog.spec: Add a second initialiser ring_init(rng) that places 1 circle near the center, 6 on a ring of radius ~0.2, 12 on a ring of radius ~0.35, and 7 on an outer ring or near the corners/edges. Jitter the angles and radii with small Gaussian noise and clip to [0.05, 0.95]. Alternate starts between hex_jitter and ring_init (even start index hex, odd start index ring). Keep SA and SLSQP as they are.
backlog.title: Ring-based init (1+6+12+7 variants)

backlog.spec: Initialise with 4 circles near the square corners at (0.12,0.12) etc., 4 medium circles at the edge midpoints, and fill the remaining 18 with a jittered hex-like lattice over the interior. Use radius-aware LP for the initial radii, then run SA and SLSQP as in the incumbent. Use this for half of the starts, with randomised corner offsets in [0.08, 0.16].
backlog.title: Corner-anchored big circles init

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, set steps=6000, T0=0.01, T1=0.0001, and sigma = 0.002 + 0.02*(T/T0). Raise the time cutoff from 120 s to 170 s. Run only 2 starts so total runtime stays under about 220 s. Choose a different point for each move: with probability 0.2 move two circles at once.
backlog.title: Slower SA with smaller moves

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP result, loop for ~10 iterations: find the circle with the smallest radius, remove it, and reinsert it at the point of the largest empty space. Find that point by evaluating a 40x40 grid and picking the point farthest from the other circles' surfaces and the walls. Then rerun the LP on the new centers, then SLSQP with maxiter 150. Accept the change if the sum improves, otherwise revert.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert worst circle

backlog.spec: Extend sa_centers with a move type chosen with probability 0.15: swap the positions of two circles with very different LP radii (the largest-radius circle and a random small one). Moves in which two circles trade places change the LP solution only if the centers are not equivalent, so use the swap together with a small jitter of 0.01 on both. Keep the Metropolis acceptance rule with the LP objective.
backlog.title: Swap sizes and neighbour moves in SA

backlog.spec: After the initial starts, spend the remaining time (until ~200 s) on iterated local search: take the best (x,y,r) solution, relocate 2-3 random circles (preferring the smallest ones) to random positions, set all radii to 0.5 of their values, run SLSQP with maxiter 200, and accept if the sum improves. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Iterated large kicks on the best state

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run L-BFGS-B on z=(x,y,r) with the objective -sum(r) + mu*(sum of squared pair overlaps max(0, ri+rj-dij)^2 + squared wall violations), with analytic gradients vectorised in numpy. Anneal mu through 10, 100, 1000, 10000, with 150 iterations each. Take the result as the SLSQP start, to cover many more starts cheaply. Use it for 20 random hex-jittered starts, then pass the best 3 to SLSQP.
backlog.title: Penalty L-BFGS with growing radii as a pre-stage

backlog.spec: Do a coarse global search with scipy differential_evolution (seeded, popsize 10, maxiter 30) over hex-row parameters: the row counts choice, row y offsets, a horizontal shift and stretch per row. The objective is the LP sum of radii of the generated centers. Use the best parameters as the init for SA and SLSQP, replacing one of the 4 starts.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over lattice parameters

backlog.spec: Record each found local optimum's sorted radii vector. In later starts, choose a new row pattern from [5,5,5,5,6], [6,5,6,5,4], [5,6,5,6,4], [4,5,6,5,6], [6,5,5,5,5] and re-draw jitter when the initial LP sum is within 1e-3 of an earlier start's. Use sigma 0.03 for later starts. Run 6 starts with SA steps reduced to 800 so that they fit in the time budget.
backlog.title: Tabu on repeated optima with a fixed layout class

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser alternative to hex_jitter: place one circle at the center, 6 on a ring of radius ~0.2, 12 on a ring of radius ~0.37, and 7 near the edges/corners (or 1+7+18 variants chosen randomly per start), then add Gaussian jitter sigma 0.02 and clip to [0.05,0.95]. Pick this initialiser for half of the starts (rng.random()<0.5) and keep the rest of the pipeline (SA, SLSQP, shrink-and-grow) unchanged. Wrap in try/except and keep the old fallback so the packing stays valid.
backlog.title: Ring-based init 1+6+12+7 with SA

backlog.spec: In sa_centers use steps=4000, T0=0.01, T1=0.0001 and sigma=0.003+0.03*(T/T0). Keep the 120s time guard but make it relative to the per-start budget (e.g. 45s per start) so every one of the 4 starts gets time. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Slower, finer SA

backlog.spec: After the multi-start loop, spend the remaining time (until about 200s from t0) on perturbing the global best solution. Each iteration moves 2-4 random circles to random positions, adds sigma=0.01 noise to all centers, sets radii to the LP radii for those centers, runs optimize() with maxiter 150, and accepts if the sum improves. Keep the best valid result. Seed the rng so runs are repeatable.
backlog.title: Iterated large kicks on best state

backlog.spec: After the best solution is found, repeat: remove the 2 circles with the smallest radii, find the largest empty holes by evaluating the distance-to-nearest-circle-surface on a 60x60 grid, place the two circles at the top two well-separated hole maxima, run LP radii and then SLSQP (maxiter 150) and accept if improved. Run until about 200s total. Cap the work so it can't exceed the time limit.
backlog.title: Remove-two-reinsert-into-holes

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP polish, run a cheap physics pre-stage: with the radii as variables, minimise -sum(r)+mu*sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 + wall violations^2) using L-BFGS-B with analytic vectorised gradients. Anneal mu over 10, 100, 1000, 1e4. Use its output as the SLSQP start in place of the LP radii. Fall back to the old start on any exception.
backlog.title: Penalty L-BFGS growing-radii pre-stage

backlog.spec: Build initial centers from a radial density: sample 26 points by Poisson-disk or best-candidate sampling in which the minimum spacing is larger near the center (about 0.22) than near the border (about 0.14). Optionally add 4 points exactly at the corners offset by 0.08. Run LP radii, SA and SLSQP as usual. Use this initialiser for 2 of the 4 starts and hex_jitter for the others.
backlog.title: Size-asymmetric init: big center, small edges

backlog.spec: Extend the sa_centers proposal: with probability 0.2 swap the positions of two circles whose LP radii differ most among near neighbours, and with probability 0.1 relocate the smallest-radius circle to a random point. The rest of the move is a Gaussian single-circle move. The LP radii are computed once per accepted state to identify the smallest and the neighbours. Keep Metropolis acceptance.
backlog.title: SA moves with neighbor swaps and radius-aware relocation

backlog.spec: Run the SLSQP in two phases per start. Phase 1 maximises sum(r) - 0.5*sum((r - rmean)^2) with analytic gradient, which discourages degenerate tiny and huge circles, for maxiter 150. Phase 2 uses the plain objective starting from the phase-1 result. Keep the best valid result and the full constraint set.
backlog.title: Soft penalty on tiny radii during SLSQP then release

backlog.spec: Replace the 4 independent SA+SLSQP starts with a population approach. Run 12 short SA chains (400 steps each) from different hex_jitter inits, rank by LP sum, and run SLSQP plus shrink-and-grow only on the top 3. Then use the remaining time for extra shrink-and-grow cycles on the best, with noise sigma drawn from {0.01,0.02,0.04}. Keep all times under 200s and a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Batch of SA chains with population selection

backlog.spec: After the existing 4-start loop (keep it unchanged, but cap its time at about 120s), run an iterated-local-search loop until about 200s total elapsed. Take the best z; repeatedly pick 2-4 random circles, relocate them to random positions in [0.05,0.95]^2 with radii set to 0.02, optimise with SLSQP (maxiter 200), and accept if the sum improves. Wrap each SLSQP call in try/except and keep the best valid result. Always finish with the existing safe_radii shrink.
backlog.title: Iterated large kicks on best state

backlog.spec: Replace the SA start with a physics pre-stage. For centers c from hex_jitter and radii r variables, minimise -sum(r)+mu*sum(overlap^2 + wall_violation^2) with L-BFGS-B (analytic gradient, vectorized over pairs) for mu in [10,100,1e3,1e4]. Then feed the result into the existing SLSQP polish. Use this for 2 of the 4 starts and keep SA for the others, so the incumbent behaviour is a fallback.
backlog.title: Penalty L-BFGS growing-radii pre-stage

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser used in 2 of the 4 starts: place 1 to 4 circles near the center, a ring of about 10 mid-sized circles, and the remaining circles on the boundary including the 4 corners. Pass these centers with matching initial radii (0.14 center, 0.11 middle, 0.08 edge) through the LP radius solve and SLSQP. Add small jitter (sigma 0.01). Other starts remain the hex_jitter + SA.
backlog.title: Big-center small-edge size-asymmetric init

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, with probability 0.2 swap the positions of two circles that have different LP radii (pick the largest and a nearby smaller one), and with probability 0.1 relocate the smallest-radius circle to a random point. Use the same LP objective and acceptance. Keep the rest of the SA identical, and keep the time limit check, so the result can only be a different trajectory.
backlog.title: SA with neighbour swap and relocation moves

backlog.spec: Run 8 short SA chains (600 steps each) from different hex_jitter starts, ranked by LP sum. Take the top 2 and polish them with SLSQP and shrink-and-grow. Replaces the 4 full starts; total SA time capped at about 100s. This gives a broader search for the same budget, and the best polished result is returned.
backlog.title: Population of SA chains with selection

backlog.spec: Change the seed from 12345 to a loop over seeds picked inside the run: the 4 starts use rng seeds 1,2,3,4 offset (e.g. default_rng(777+start)). Extend the row patterns in hex_jitter with [5,6,5,6,4] and [6,5,5,5,5] chosen uniformly among 4 patterns, each with 26 points. Verify the sums equal 26 locally.
backlog.title: Different seeds and row patterns sweep

backlog.spec: In the first SLSQP call for each start, add a lower bound r_i >= 0.04 on the variables, solve, then re-solve with the lower bound removed (bounds back to (0,0.5)) starting from that solution. This avoids early collapse of circles to zero radius. Keep the shrink-and-grow cycles afterwards.
backlog.title: Soft tiny-radius penalty then release

backlog.spec: After the incumbent pipeline, run basin hopping with a safe design: perturb the best z by Gaussian noise sigma drawn from {0.01,0.03,0.06} on all centers, shrink radii by 0.7, run SLSQP maxiter 150 inside try/except, and accept if the sum is higher (or by Metropolis with T=0.002). Return the best state. Always fall back to the incumbent result and check finiteness.
backlog.title: Basin-hop with trust-region SLSQP warm perturbation

backlog.spec: After picking the best centers, solve the LP for radii with the centers fixed (lp_radii), then subtract 1e-12 from each radius and clip at zero, then run the pairwise check in double precision. Use whichever of the LP result and the SLSQP radii has the larger sum after the validity check. This is a cheap, no-risk finishing step that recovers about 1e-9 of margin.
backlog.title: Final feasibility-exact radius polish

backlog.spec: After the existing multi-start loop, spend the remaining time (stop by 200s total) on basin hopping from the best (centers, radii). Each iteration: pick 2-4 random circles, relocate them to random positions in [0.05,0.95]^2 with a small radius, add Gaussian noise sigma 0.01 to all centers, run lp_radii then optimize() (SLSQP maxiter 150). Accept if the sum improves, otherwise revert. Seeded rng. Keep the final safe_radii shrink and fall back to the previous best if anything is non-finite.
backlog.title: Iterated large kicks on best state

backlog.spec: For the best solution found, repeat: remove the 2 smallest-radius circles, find the 2 largest empty holes by sampling 20000 random points and computing the max distance-to-nearest-circle-surface (greedy, second hole must be away from the first), place the circles there with small radii, run optimize() with SLSQP. Accept if the sum improves. Run this loop until about 60s are used. Wrap each attempt in try/except and keep a valid best.
backlog.title: Remove-two reinsert into largest holes

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that places the 26 centers by radial rule: 1 point near (0.5,0.5), then points on concentric rings with jitter. Give the initial radii as a decreasing function of the distance from the centre, from about 0.14 at the centre to 0.07 near the edges, and also include 4 corner points at (0.07,0.07) etc. Use these radii and centers as the SLSQP start (skip the LP radii step) for 2 of the 4 starts, with the others unchanged. Then SA is not applied to these starts, only the shrink-and-grow cycles.
backlog.title: Size-asymmetric init: big centre, small edges

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, with probability 0.2 replace the Gaussian move by a relocation: take the circle with the smallest LP radius and move it to a random point in the square. With probability 0.1 swap the positions of two nearby circles (distance < 0.25) and add jitter 0.01. Keep the LP objective and the Metropolis rule. Use steps=2500, and keep the time guard at 120s.
backlog.title: SA with neighbour-swap and relocate moves

backlog.spec: Before SA, generate each start by a simple force simulation. Random centers, radii start at 0.02. For 300 iterations: grow all radii by 3% (capped so that the sum is <=2.7), compute pairwise overlaps and wall overlaps, move the centers along the overlap resolution (the vectorised displacement is proportional to the overlap, step 0.5), and clip to [r,1-r]. Then pass the centers to the existing SA and SLSQP pipeline. Seeded. Replace hex_jitter on 2 of the 4 starts only.
backlog.title: Physics repulsion with growing radii init

backlog.spec: After the best SLSQP result, run scipy minimize with method trust-constr from it. Use only the pair constraints for pairs with centre distance < 1.5*(ri+rj)+0.05, expressed as NonlinearConstraint with analytic sparse jacobian, plus bounds. Use xtol 1e-12 and maxiter 500, limited to 40s. Accept the result only if, after safe_radii, the sum is higher than the current best.
backlog.title: Trust-constr polish with sparse neighbour constraints

backlog.spec: Change the master seed per start (seeds 1..4 derived from 12345+start*7919) and force the row pattern cycling through [5,5,5,5,6], [6,5,6,5,4], [5,6,5,6,4], [4,5,5,6,6] (all sum to 26) so that every start uses a different lattice. Raise the jitter sigma to 0.03 on alternate starts. Reduce the SA steps to 1200 so that 5 starts fit within the time budget.
backlog.title: Multiple seeds with different row patterns per start

backlog.spec: In the shrink-and-grow loop replace the uniform 0.9 radius shrinkage by a nonuniform one: multiply each radius by a random factor in [0.6,1.0], and push each center away from its nearest neighbour by 0.01-0.03. Then run optimize(). Increase the cycles to 20 while time permits (stop at 170s). This diversifies the local rearrangements compared with the uniform shrink.
backlog.title: Soft-pruned SLSQP with constraint warm-up on radii shrink

backlog.spec: After the final best, run a cheap local search of 1500 iterations purely with lp_radii. Each iteration picks a circle, moves it by Gaussian sigma 0.003, evaluates the LP sum, and accepts it if it is better (greedy hill climbing, with sigma adapted: x1.1 on success, x0.97 on failure). Run on the best state, then do one last SLSQP optimize() and the safe_radii shrink. It is cheap, with an LP per step of about 5ms.
backlog.title: Pairwise radius-transfer moves via LP on perturbed centers

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser using a 5x5 square-ish layout of 25 points with the rows offset alternately by 0.5 spacing and compress vertical spacing, then add the 26th point at the position of the largest hole. Use jitter sigma 0.015, and a random choice of which row is shifted. Use it for two of the four starts alongside hex_jitter, with the same SA and SLSQP pipeline.
backlog.title: Corner-and-edge lattice-with-defect init

backlog.spec: After the existing multi-start loop, take the best solution (centers, radii). Repeat until about 200s elapsed: pick two circles with clearly different radii that are near neighbours (distance < 1.3*(ri+rj)), swap their centers, then run optimize() from the swapped state (radii taken from a fresh lp_radii call, scaled by 0.9). Accept only if the sum improves. Keep the best valid result and the existing safe_radii final step. Wrap every step in try/except so a failure falls back to the incumbent. Guard with the time check so total runtime stays under 230s.
backlog.title: Basin-hop from best with neighbour-swap radius moves

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that places 1 to 4 circles near the centre region (random within [0.35,0.65]) and the remaining circles on a jittered hex-row layout, with starting radii r0 decreasing with distance from the centre (0.16 at the centre down to 0.06 at the edges). Feed these radii and centres directly into optimize() (skip the SA stage for these starts, or use a short SA of 300 steps). Use this for 2 of the 4 starts and hex_jitter for the others. Make sure the incumbent path still runs so the result is never worse.
backlog.title: Size-asymmetric init: big centre, small edges

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP in each start, run 3 SLSQP stages that maximise a concave surrogate sum(r_i^p) with p = 0.5, then 0.8, then 1.0 (objective -sum(r**p), gradient -p*r**(p-1) with r clipped at 1e-6). Early stages favour equalising radii and so spread circles; the last stage is the true objective. Each stage warm-starts from the previous with maxiter 150. Keep the best-by-true-sum solution.
backlog.title: Continuation on the radii-sum objective with p-norm

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent pipeline unchanged but run it for a list of seeds (e.g. 1,2,3,...) and alternate among the row patterns [5,5,5,5,6], [6,5,6,5,4], [4,5,6,5,6], [5,6,5,6,4] by start index, with time-aware looping until 200s total. Reduce SA steps to 800 per start so that about 8 starts fit. Take the best valid one. This is a pure diversity change relative to the incumbent.
backlog.title: Seed and row-pattern sweep with many short starts

backlog.spec: Initialise with 4 circles at the corners (centres at (0.1,0.1) etc.) and 4 at edge midpoints, then fill the interior with 18 points from a hex lattice of spacing about 0.19 with random removal of surplus points and jitter 0.02. Run the SA + SLSQP pipeline on it. Use this for half of the starts, alternating with hex_jitter, and keep the best valid solution.
backlog.title: Corner-circle-fixed lattice with defects

backlog.spec: After the best SLSQP result, identify active constraints (pairs with distance - ri - rj < 1e-6 and wall contacts with slack < 1e-6). Solve the KKT-like equality system via scipy.optimize.least_squares or fsolve on (x, y, r) with those constraints as equalities, starting from the best solution. If the result is feasible (all constraints satisfied to 1e-12) and the sum is higher, use it. Then shrink radii by 1e-12 and verify. Fall back otherwise.
backlog.title: Active-set LP/Newton polish of the final contacts

backlog.spec: After the multi-start loop, run a loop from the best solution: shake all centers by Gaussian noise sigma cycling through [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.04], shrink radii by 0.8, and run SLSQP with maxiter 200. Accept if better than the best. Also on every 5th iteration relocate the single smallest circle to a random point. Time-limit the loop to 100s using the budget left after the starts (reduce the starts to 2).
backlog.title: Perturbation of best with growing kick schedule

backlog.spec: For the best solution, for each circle i in turn (in order of increasing radius), remove it, compute the 3 best candidate points via grid sampling (60x60 grid, choose points maximising the free-space radius), reinsert it at each candidate, run lp_radii on the full set, and keep the candidate if the total sum improves. Follow with a short SLSQP (maxiter 100). Repeat 2 passes. Time-guard it, with try/except.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise exact LP-guided greedy move of one circle

backlog.spec: In the first SLSQP of each start add a term to the objective, -sum(r) + lam*sum(max(0, 0.04-r)**2) with lam=50 and its analytic gradient, so that no circle collapses to a tiny radius. Then rerun optimize() with lam=0 from that result. Compare to the unpenalised path and keep the better.
backlog.title: Soft tiny-radius penalty then release

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 38 pipeline unchanged but change the seed in np.random.default_rng(12345) to a different fixed value (e.g. 777), and loop over 3 seeds only if the time guard allows. Reduce each start's SA time cap so the total stays under 200 s. Keep the best result across starts. This tests how much of the score is seed luck.

backlog.spec: After the best SLSQP result, identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-7, wall gaps < 1e-7). Solve the nonlinear system of equalities (active pair distances equal r_i+r_j, wall contacts equal r_i) with a few Gauss-Newton or lstsq steps, using np.linalg.lstsq with min-norm updates. Accept only if the sum increases and all constraints hold. Then apply the safe_radii shrink at 1e-12.
backlog.title: Contact-graph polish via Newton on active set

backlog.title: Two-size-class lattice init

backlog.title: Corner-pinned SA

backlog.title: Parallel tempering SA

backlog.title: Radius-sum exponent continuation

Keep the best result over starts. Goal is a lucky basin, with no invalid output from timeouts.

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, change the move probabilities: swap of the largest circle with a near neighbour from 0.2 to 0.35, and smallest-circle relocation from 0.1 to 0.05. Everything else is unchanged. Tests whether more size-swap moves help the basin search.
backlog.title: Swap probability retune

backlog.spec: After the first SA on each start, run a second sa_centers pass from the returned best centers with T0=0.004, T1=0.0003 and 1000 steps (a reheat), before the SLSQP. Keep the time guards. This refines the best layout with the LP objective rather than starting over.

Use a strict time guard (stop at 200 s total) and re-check validity with safe_radii. Cut the number of starts to 3 to leave the time.

Keep total LP evaluations about equal to the current budget (about 1500*4 per start) and respect the 120 s time guard.

Use it for 2 of the 4 starts in place of hex_jitter, followed by the usual SA and SLSQP.

Finish with SLSQP from the improved state and keep it if better.
backlog.title: Contact-graph perturbation via LP greedy

backlog.spec: Before each start's final SLSQP, run SLSQP stages maximizing sum(r_i^p) with p=0.5, then 0.8, then 1.0 (gradient p*r^(p-1) with r clipped at 1e-6), maxiter 100 each, warm-starting from the previous stage. The concave early stages favour more equal radii and push away from degenerate tiny circles. Keep the SLSQP constraint code unchanged. Apply to starts 0 and 1 only.
backlog.title: p-norm radius continuation

backlog.spec: Change the master seed and make each start use its own rng seeded default_rng(1000+17*start), run up to 6 starts but stop launching new starts after 150 s elapsed, each SA capped at 1200 steps. Keep the SA move set of the incumbent. Select best across starts.

This diversifies the basins handed to SLSQP at small extra cost.
backlog.title: SA objective with soft overlap-free radii via SLSQP-lite

backlog.spec: Init with 4 corner points, 12 points evenly spaced along a square ring at inset 0.1 (3 per side excluding corners), and 10 points on a jittered hex arrangement inside the central [0.25,0.75] region, jitter sigma 0.02. Use for 2 of the 4 starts, with SA then SLSQP as usual. Differs from earlier corner-anchored attempt by having no preset radii and by feeding SA.
backlog.title: Boundary-ring plus interior init

Keep swap and relocate moves and the temperature schedule unchanged.

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-7, wall gaps < 1e-7). Solve the KKT system for the sum-of-radii maximisation restricted to those active constraints with a few Newton/lstsq steps on (x,y,r), using the LP duals as multipliers. Accept the result only if every constraint is still satisfied after a 1e-12 safe shrink and the sum increases; otherwise keep the original. Wrap everything in try/except.
backlog.title: Contact-graph Newton polish

backlog.spec: Keep the slot 38 script as the baseline and run it with seed 12345 for the first start. Wrap each later start with try/except and a per-start time budget of 45 s. Verify the validity of the final packing (pair distances and walls) before returning. If the best result is invalid, fall back to the best valid earlier start. backlog.spec: Add an initialiser that places about 4 large circles (radius guess 0.14) on a 2x2 arrangement near the middle and fills the rest with 22 small circles on a hex-ish lattice of spacing about 0.17 that skips lattice sites overlapping the large circles. Take the 26 sites closest to a jittered fill, then apply sa_centers and SLSQP. Use this for start 1 only and keep hex_jitter for the others.
backlog.title: Two-size-class lattice with defect init

backlog.spec: For the first SLSQP solve in each start, add the penalty -1e-3*sum(log(r+1e-3)) to the objective, with its analytic gradient, to discourage circles collapsing to zero. Then re-run SLSQP with the plain objective from that solution. Use the plain result only if it is better than the penalised result.
backlog.title: Soft tiny-radius penalty then release

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP in each start, run SLSQP on the objective -sum(r^p), where p goes 0.5, then 0.8, then 1.0 and each stage starts from the previous solution. This is a variant of the slot 56 idea with a gentler ladder. Keep the stage only if the final sum improves over direct SLSQP.
backlog.title: p-norm radius continuation

backlog.spec: Cut the SA to 1000 steps for each of 8 hex_jitter starts, giving each its own time cap. Rank the results by LP sum, then run the full 1500-step SA plus SLSQP only on the top 2. Keep the per-start budgets so that the total stays under 200 s.
backlog.title: Two-pass SA with elite restarts

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser with 12 circles evenly spaced along the boundary at inset about 0.08 (corners included), and 14 interior circles laid out as a jittered 4-row hex. Use it for odd starts and hex_jitter for even starts, then run SA and SLSQP as before.
backlog.title: Boundary-ring plus interior init

This differs from slot 46 in that it is a rare move, so the existing 10% uniform random relocation stays unchanged.
backlog.title: SA with LP-radius-aware relocation to Voronoi-like holes

backlog.spec: After the shrink-and-grow cycles, run optimize on the best state once more with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-15. Use the result only if the sum improves and it passes a validity check. Then use safe_radii with a 1e-12 margin instead of 1e-9 (verify the validity of the packing first).
backlog.title: Final-stage SLSQP with tight ftol and more iterations

Wrap construct_packing so that every stage checks a global deadline (t0+200s), and wrap the final result in a validity check: recompute radii with safe_radii, verify the bounds and pairwise constraints in double precision, and if invalid fall back to the best valid packing seen so far (keep a running best valid packing after each SLSQP). This makes later bolder edits robust. Keep the slot 38 algorithm unchanged otherwise.

Then run the usual sa_centers with a lower T0=0.008 and SLSQP. Uses the incumbent move set. Gives an exploit-focused restart.

backlog.title: Row-pattern init for 26 as 4-5-6-5-6 offset lattice

backlog.title: SA objective with tiny-radius penalty

backlog.title: Two-ring-of-SLSQP: warm repeat with ftol loosening

backlog.title: Architecture: fix four corner circles as radius-heavy in SA via LP weights

Keep 20% total probability. Fall back to a Gaussian move if no candidate exists.

Guard with a time check so total runtime stays under 230 s.

Rows are placed the same way, and the jitter sigma stays 0.02. Keep the first start on the original pattern so the incumbent trajectory is preserved in start 0.

For starts 1..5 use fresh rngs default_rng(5000+start) and sa steps 1000 with the same T schedule, and stop the loop when 170 s of wall clock is exceeded. Select best by final SLSQP value. This preserves the incumbent result as a floor while adding diversity.

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent loop for starts 0..3 unchanged and consuming the shared rng. After it, if elapsed time < 120 s, run additional starts with independent default_rng(9000+k) for hex_jitter and SA, each with a time check so every start begins only if elapsed < 150 s and SA is capped to finish within the 200 s mark. Only replace the best if strictly better. This cannot lower the score below the incumbent.
backlog.title: Start 0 preserved plus extra starts using fresh rngs

Implement via a weights argument to lp_radii (c = -w) and report the unweighted sum for acceptance in the final phase. Smooths the landscape to escape local optima.

Accept if improved. This opens room for rearrangement of interior circles while leaving the boundary structure intact.
backlog.title: Corner-pinned radii bonus in final shrink-and-grow

Wrap in time guards and exact validity checks, and keep the incumbent if nothing improves.

Pass the result to SLSQP. The step is cheap and vectorised and nudges the SA centers into a slightly less jammed configuration.
backlog.title: Quadratic-penalty hinge smoothing to SLSQP warm start

backlog.spec: Many recent edits scored -0.0000, which is likely timeouts. Add a global deadline helper (time.time()-t0) and make every start's SA and shrink-and-grow loop stop early so total runtime stays under about 200 s. Also wrap the final result in a try/except that falls back to the best valid packing found so far. Keep the incumbent algorithm and seed (12345) unchanged otherwise. The aim is robustness, so later edits don't fail by timeout.
backlog.title: Safe wall-clock guard with SA step cap

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, change the thresholds so the largest-circle swap branch runs when u<0.12, the smallest-circle relocation when 0.12<=u<0.20, and Gaussian single-circle moves otherwise. Leave everything else identical to the incumbent (seed 12345, 4 starts, 1500 SA steps). This is a small retune of the incumbent's move mix.
backlog.title: Lower swap probability to 12%, relocate 8%

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, score each candidate as sum(r) minus 0.02*sum(max(0, 0.04 - r)) to discourage near-zero circles that trap the search. Use the penalised value for acceptance only. Track the best by the true sum. Keep the final SLSQP unchanged.
backlog.title: SA objective with tiny-radius floor penalty

backlog.spec: Add an SA move (10% probability, taken from the Gaussian branch) that picks a random circle i and its nearest neighbour j with a different LP radius and swaps their centres. Then add Gaussian noise of sigma 0.01 to both. This differs from the incumbent's swap, which uses the largest circle. Keep the remaining move mix unchanged.
backlog.title: Pair-swap of two random neighbouring circles in SA

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, build the set of pairs with distance < (ri+rj)*1.05+1e-3. Rerun SLSQP with only those pair constraints plus the boundary constraints, ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 500. Accept the result only if its sum rises and the full pairwise check passes. Then apply the 1e-12 shrink. Fall back to the unpolished result otherwise.
backlog.title: Final-stage SLSQP on active contacts with tight ftol

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser for odd starts that places 4 larger seed circles in a 2x2 pattern near (0.3,0.3), (0.7,0.3), (0.3,0.7) and (0.7,0.7). Fill the remaining 22 points with a jittered hex lattice that avoids a radius-0.12 disc around each seed (rejection sampling with min spacing 0.14). Then run the usual SA and SLSQP. Even starts keep hex_jitter, and start 0 stays identical.
backlog.title: Two-size-class lattice start

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP, identify the active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT-like system with scipy.optimize.root or lstsq, so these gaps go to exactly zero while the multipliers stay nonnegative. Accept only if the sum rises and the validity check passes. Apply the shrink afterwards.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton contact polish

backlog.spec: After the 4 starts, spend at most 40 s of wall time on this loop. Perturb 3 random circles of the best centres by sigma 0.05 and run lp_radii. Run a short 150-step SA at low T (T0=0.002). Then run a 100-iteration SLSQP. Keep the result if it improves. Check time.time() before every SLSQP call. Return the incumbent best if nothing improves, so that the output cannot be worse.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from best with SA-sized kicks, time-capped

backlog.spec: Before the final SLSQP of each start, run SLSQP with objective -sum(r**p) for p=0.6 and then p=0.85, using maxiter 100 each, warm-started from the previous stage. Finish with p=1 as in the incumbent. Concave p favours equalising the radii, which may reveal different contact graphs. Keep SA unchanged.
backlog.title: p-norm radius continuation before final SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep the 4 incumbent starts exactly as they are (same rng stream). Then, if time remains under 150 s, run 2 more starts using a separate rng default_rng(999) so the original rng stream is not disturbed. Return the best of all starts. This cannot be worse than the incumbent given the time guard.
backlog.title: Extra start from SA with different seed, kept only if better

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify circles with fewer than 3 touching neighbours or walls (rattlers, contact tolerance 1e-7). Relocate each rattler to the centre of the largest empty circle found via a 200x200 grid distance field, run SLSQP with maxiter 200 from the result, and keep it only if the sum improves. Guard by the wall clock (stop at 200 s from t0) and keep the final safe_radii shrink.
backlog.title: Contact-graph rattler removal and re-solve

backlog.spec: In sa_centers change the swap branch threshold from u<0.2 to u<0.12 and the relocate branch from u<0.3 to u<0.2, leaving everything else identical to the incumbent (same seed, same starts, same time guards). This is a small SA tweak around the incumbent's move mix.
backlog.title: Lower swap probability to 12% with relocate 8%

backlog.spec: Give each of the 4 starts a fixed SA time budget of 30 s via a per-start t_start passed to sa_centers (break when time.time()-t_start>30) instead of the global 120 s cutoff measured from t0, so later starts are never starved. Keep steps=1500 and all else the same, and keep total runtime under 200 s.
backlog.title: SA step cap per start with time-share

backlog.spec: In hex_jitter, after jittering, push points whose x or y is within 0.12 of the boundary 30% of the way toward the boundary (to 0.06 clip distance), so boundary circles start near walls. Only applied to starts 1..3; start 0 stays as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Edge-biased SA jitter initialiser

backlog.spec: In sa_centers add a rare (5%) move that takes a random circle and a second random circle and sets the second to the mirror image of the first across the square's main diagonal or vertical midline, followed by the usual LP evaluation and Metropolis acceptance. This encourages symmetric partial structures seen in good packings.
backlog.title: Reflection-symmetric SA moves

backlog.spec: In sa_centers evaluate candidates with the LP objective sum(r_i) minus 0.002*sum(r_i^2)-style variance penalty (computed on the LP solution, no extra LP), which favours more balanced radii in the SA energy. Final selection and SLSQP stay with the plain sum.
backlog.title: Equal-weight LP radii exponent in SA objective

backlog.spec: In sa_centers compute radii by LP with the neighbour constraint right-hand side d*1.01 for acceptance only (soft slack), then rescale to the true feasible LP for best tracking every 50 accepted moves. This smooths the energy landscape so that SA crosses barriers more easily.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant SA objective

backlog.spec: After each SA returns centers and before SLSQP, perform 2 sweeps over circles in random order, trying 8 shifts of 0.01 in compass directions for each circle and accepting any that increase the LP sum. Limit to 20 s per start with a time guard.
backlog.title: Greedy exact LP coordinate sweep after SA

backlog.spec: Replace the single geometric cooling in sa_centers with 3 sawtooth cycles within the same step budget: each cycle cools from T0 (decreasing 0.02, 0.012, 0.007) to T1, and the state resets to the best-so-far at the start of each cycle. Total steps remain 1500.
backlog.title: Anneal SA temperature with reheat cycles

backlog.spec: In the shrink-and-grow loop, instead of scaling all radii by 0.9, scale by 0.95 and additionally scale the 3 smallest circles to 0.5 times their radius and displace each by N(0,0.05). Accept only if the sum improves, as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Larger random shrink on the weakest region before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a new initialiser used for odd-numbered starts: build a full 6-row hexagonal lattice of 6 points per row (alternating offset, 36 points scaled to fill the unit square with margin 0.08), then delete 10 points chosen at random (seeded rng), add Gaussian jitter sigma 0.01, and pass to the existing SA then SLSQP pipeline. Keep start 0 and all other code identical, keep the 1e-9 safe shrink and the time guards.
backlog.title: Hex lattice with removed circles init

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, in the last 20% of steps, replace the random relocation branch with: find circles with LP radius below 0.5*median radius, and move one of them to the point (among 300 random samples) maximising min distance to other centres and walls. Accept via the usual Metropolis rule. Earlier phases stay unchanged so the incumbent behaviour is preserved for 80% of the run.
backlog.title: SA final-phase greedy relocation of rattlers

backlog.spec: Before the shrink-and-grow cycles in each start, add to optimize() an optional set of linear inequality constraints r_i >= r_j for pairs (i,j) taken from the current radius ordering of the 6 largest circles (chain r_(1)>=r_(2)>=...). Solve once with these constraints to break symmetry and avoid zero-radius solutions, then release them and re-solve normally. Keep the best of both.
backlog.title: Lexicographic SLSQP with radius-ordering constraints

backlog.spec: Within each start, after SA, instead of one SLSQP from the best SA centres, run SLSQP with maxiter 60 from the best SA state and from 3 lightly jittered copies (sigma 0.003); then run the full 300-iteration SLSQP only on the best of the four. Respect the time guards and leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Cheap SLSQP screening of SA output

backlog.spec: Generate the initial hex_jitter centres by sampling 13 points, reflecting them across x=0.5 to get 26, ensuring none lie on the axis by shifting by 0.02; use it for start 1 only, then run the normal unconstrained SA and SLSQP so symmetry can break. Start 0 stays exactly as in the incumbent.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric SA init only

backlog.spec: Wrap optimize() so that bounds on x,y are tightened to z0 +/- 0.08 (clipped to [0,1]) in a first pass with maxiter 150, then rerun with the full [0,1] bounds from the result. This local-trust-region two-pass reduces wild SLSQP jumps after the SA. Apply to all starts; keep other code unchanged.
backlog.title: SLSQP with analytic trust bound on step

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, make the acceptance objective v = sum(radii) + 0.02*min over circles of radius... replaced by a tie-break: v = sum(radii) - 0.001*number of circles with radius < 0.02, anneal this coefficient to 0 over the last 30% of steps. Purpose is to discourage dead circles early without changing the final objective.
backlog.title: Late-start SA with LP radius objective using top-weighted tie-breaker

backlog.spec: Add a 8% SA move that picks a random circle and its nearest neighbour, rotates the pair by a random angle in [-0.5,0.5] rad around their midpoint, and evaluates with the LP. Take the probability mass from the plain Gaussian branch only, leaving swap at 20% and relocate at 10%.
backlog.title: Neighbour-pair rotation move in SA

backlog.spec: After start 0 finishes, for start 1 and 2 initialise the SA from the start-0 best centres perturbed by Gaussian sigma 0.04 on 6 random circles, and run sa_centers with T0=0.006 instead of 0.02 and 1500 steps. Keep start 3 as the incumbent hex_jitter start. Report the best over all starts.
backlog.title: Restart seeds from perturbed SA best with cooler temperature

backlog.spec: Measure the time per lp_radii call over the first 50 SA steps of start 0, then set steps for every start so that the 4 starts use about 170 s total of SA (steps = budget/4/t_per_call), capped at 6000, rather than fixed 1500. Retain the 120 s per-call guard and the final safe shrink. Fixed T0 and T1 stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Wall-clock-scaled SA step count

backlog.spec: After the incumbent pipeline finishes, take the best packing and run a time-capped loop (stop at 200 s of wall time from t0). Each iteration: pick a random circle, move its centre to a random point (or the centre of the largest empty hole found by sampling 500 random points and picking the one with greatest distance-minus-radius clearance), set all radii to 0.5 of their values, run the existing optimize() SLSQP with maxiter 150, and accept only if the sum improves. Keep the best state. Return it with the existing safe_radii shrink. The incumbent result must be returned if nothing improves.
backlog.title: Contact-graph perturbation: delete and re-add one contact

backlog.spec: After choosing the best packing, build a reduced SLSQP that uses only the pair constraints with slack (distance - ri - rj) < 0.02 plus the wall constraints for circles within 0.02 of a wall. Run it with ftol 1e-15 and maxiter 500 starting from the best z. Verify with a full double-precision check that all pairs and walls are satisfied after multiplying radii by (1-1e-12). Accept only if the sum rises above the incumbent sum. This gains the last 1e-7 to 1e-5 of the sum.
backlog.title: Final high-precision SLSQP with active-pair constraints only

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent 4 starts exactly as they are, including the seed and the rng sequence. Then, while time.time()-t0 < 150, run additional starts using a separate rng, default_rng(99), each with a 600-step SA (T0=0.015, T1=0.0005) from hex_jitter followed by one SLSQP optimize() and 2 shrink-and-grow cycles. Replace the best only if strictly better. A separate rng keeps the first 4 starts unchanged, so the result cannot be worse than the incumbent.
backlog.title: Wall-clock-scaled extra SA starts using leftover time

backlog.spec: Add an initialiser for odd extra starts. Build a 5x5 square-ish lattice of centres with spacing 0.2 offset by 0.1. Replace one 2x2 block near a random interior location with a single point at the block centre, and add 2 extra circles placed in the largest holes (found by sampling 2000 random points and taking the max min-distance). Jitter with sigma 0.01, run SA and SLSQP. Square lattice with defects covers a different basin family than hex rows. Run it as start 4 only if time remains, and keep it only if it is better.
backlog.title: Two-size-class lattice with defect init

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, use the LP objective with per-circle weights w_i = 1 + 0.5*(1 - frac)*(rank_i/n - 0.5) in the first half of the cooling, where rank_i is the rank of the LP radius. This penalises size concentration early, then falls back to uniform weights, so the final accepted values are comparable. Recompute cur_v when the weights change at each 10% step so the acceptance comparison stays consistent. Evaluate the true sum of radii for best tracking.
backlog.title: p-norm radius continuation inside SA objective

backlog.spec: After the SA, for the best centres, do a systematic exhaustive pass: for each pair (i,j) among the 8 nearest-neighbour pairs of the largest circle, swap the positions of i and j, compute the LP sum, and keep any strict improvement. Then for each circle, try nudging it by 0.01 in 8 directions with LP evaluation, accepting improvements, for 3 sweeps. Do this on the SA output of every start before SLSQP. The LP is cheap, and the sweep is deterministic.
backlog.title: Targeted two-circle swap exploring size permutation with fixed centres

backlog.spec: Use one extra rng, default_rng(2024), solely for the SA moves in starts 1 to 3, leaving hex_jitter draws on the original rng so the initial layouts are identical to the incumbent's. The incumbent's SA has noise sequences that may be unlucky for starts 1 to 3. Keep start 0 identical. Report the best of all. This isolates SA stochasticity from the initial-layout stochasticity.
backlog.title: Seed run from a different rng stream for SA only

backlog.spec: Build an init in which 4 corner circles of radius about 0.12 are placed at (r,r) style positions, then 12 edge circles of radius about 0.1 are placed 3 per side between the corners at equal spacing offset inward by 0.1, and the remaining 10 circles go into the interior on a jittered 3-3-4 staggered pattern of radius about 0.12. Feed the centres to lp_radii and then SLSQP directly, with no SA, as a single extra start after the 4 incumbent starts. Take it only if better.
backlog.title: Bolder: layered boundary-first construction

backlog.spec: In the shrink-and-grow cycles, replace the full 0..1 bounds on centres with bounds of +-0.08 around the cycle's start point and radii bounds [0, 0.5]. This limits SLSQP to explore locally, preventing it from collapsing circles to zero, which gives -0.0000 style failures. Also increase the cycles from 8 to 14 only while time.time()-t0 < 170. Accept an improved sum only.
backlog.title: SLSQP trust-bounded step via variable bounds around warm start

backlog.spec: In shrink-and-grow cycles, rather than multiplying all radii by 0.9, multiply only the 8 smallest radii by 0.3 and add Gaussian noise of sigma 0.03 to the centres of those 8 circles only, leaving the others unperturbed. Then run optimize(). This frees the small interstitial circles to find better holes while the large-circle skeleton stays in place. Use it for cycles of odd index and keep the original perturbation for even index cycles.
backlog.title: Tempered shrink: shrink only the smallest 8 circles

backlog.spec: After the multi-start loop finishes (guard: only if elapsed < 150 s), run a basin-hopping loop on the best packing with a hard wall-clock stop at 200 s total from t0. Each iteration: pick 2 random circles, move them to random points, set all radii to 0.5x LP radii, run optimize() with maxiter 100, accept only if the sum improves. Wrap everything in try/except and fall back to the incumbent result. Never let the final result be worse than the incumbent, and always apply safe_radii. Earlier basin-hopping attempts scored 0 because of timeouts, so check time before every solve.
backlog.title: Basin-hop with safe time cap on best contact graph

backlog.spec: Many past edits scored -0.0000, which means timeouts or invalid output. Wrap each multi-start in try/except and a time check (skip the start if elapsed > 170 s). Keep the best valid packing so far. Before returning, verify in double precision that all circles are inside the square and no pairs overlap. If a check fails, shrink radii by 1e-9 and recheck, repeating up to 5 times. Leave the algorithm otherwise identical to the incumbent. This makes later experiments safe to combine.
backlog.title: Robust fallback wrapper for zero-score failures

backlog.spec: In sa_centers, replace the objective sum(r) with sum(r) + 0.02*sum(min(r, 0.12)) so there is a mild bonus for the number of medium-size circles. Use this only for acceptance. Track the best state by true sum(r) and return that. After SA the SLSQP stage optimises the true objective, so there is no bias in the output.
backlog.title: Ensemble LP-weighted SA objective

backlog.spec: Add a new initialiser: a 6x5 offset hex lattice (30 sites) in the unit square, with 4 random sites removed, jitter sigma 0.015. Use it for start index 2 only (starts 0, 1 and 3 stay unchanged). Run the normal SA and SLSQP pipeline on it. Keep the best result across starts.
backlog.title: Hex lattice with two vacancies and compression init

backlog.spec: For starts 1 and 3 only, before the first SLSQP, run a short SLSQP (maxiter 80) with all radii tied to a single variable r, maximised over the centres. Then release the radii by starting from LP radii on the resulting centres and run the normal SLSQP. Guard with try/except. Cap this at 20 s per start.
backlog.title: Two-phase SLSQP with equal-radius inflation

backlog.spec: After the multi-start loop, run a 40 s localized SA from the best centres. Each move perturbs only circles within distance 0.25 of one of the 5 smallest-radius circles, with sigma 0.01 and a low temperature (T0=0.002, T1=0.0002). The objective is the LP sum. Re-solve with SLSQP at the end, and keep the result only if it improves. Respect the 4-minute limit.
backlog.title: Late SA restricted to the smallest-circle neighbourhood

backlog.spec: Run 12 short SA chains (300 steps each, 6 s cap each) from hex_jitter initialisations with distinct seeds. Rank them by LP sum. Then run the full 1500-step SA and SLSQP only on the top 2, followed by the existing shrink-and-grow loop. Keep the best result across all. Use a fixed seed. Unlike the earlier population idea, this keeps the full-length SA for the finalists and drops start 0's guaranteed run.
backlog.title: Dual-seed parallel-structure batch of cheap SA screens

backlog.spec: Initialise SLSQP radii for hex starts not from LP but from a size profile: r = 0.11 for circles whose centre is within 0.25 of the centre of the square, and 0.08 for the rest. Use this on start 3 only, with the SA centres unchanged. Run the normal SLSQP and shrink-and-grow steps afterwards.
backlog.title: Row structure with differing circle-size layers

backlog.spec: In optimize(), run a two-step schedule for the shrink-and-grow cycles. First solve with the pair constraint relaxed to d^2 >= (ri+rj)^2 - eps, eps=0.002. Then solve with eps=0 from that result. The first solve lets the circles pass through each other and escape local traps. Accept if the final sum improves.
backlog.title: Annealed overlap-allowed SLSQP with growing penalty

backlog.spec: For start 1, take start 0's final centres and apply one of the square's 8 symmetries combined with swapping the 6 largest circles to different positions chosen at random. Run SA at low temperature (T0=0.005) for 600 steps, then SLSQP and shrink-and-grow. This explores new basins near the best structure rather than restarting from scratch.
backlog.title: Quality-diverse restarts via center-of-mass rotation

incumbent.description: Adds an annealed-overlap SLSQP step to each shrink-and-grow cycle: a first solve with the pair constraints relaxed by eps=0.002 lets circles pass through each other, then an exact (eps=0) solve starts from that result, and the cycle is kept only if the final sum improves.

memo:
Incumbent is slot 38 at -2.6360, past the 2.635 target. Slot 136 tied it at -2.6360 and was accepted, but it did not improve the score. Roughly 100 slots since slot 38 have not beaten it, so this is a plateau.

Helped: seeded multi-start SLSQP (-2.6130), jittered hex-row init (-2.6261), SA over centres (-2.6304), and SA swap plus smallest-circle relocation moves (-2.6360).

Did not help: other inits (ring, radial, corner, big-centre); penalty pre-stages; slower or reheated SA; parallel tempering (-1.1282); differential evolution; more starts; polish steps (all unchanged at -2.6304 or -2.6360). Many -0.0000 results, e.g. basin hopping in slots 41 and 50, probably mean timeouts or invalid packings.

Next: stop proposing repeats, since many were aborted. Try only untested small tweaks, such as other relocation fractions, and keep runs under 4 minutes with the safe radius shrink.
